stories.title: Colombia quake death toll surpasses 240
stories.summary: The death toll from Monday’s 7.4-magnitude earthquake in western Colombia has risen to more than 200, as rescuers race against time to find survivors trapped beneath collapsed buildings. On Tuesday, a 32-year-old woman was pulled alive from the rubble, but many others remain missing. The disaster is the first major challenge for President Abelardo de la Espriella, who was inaugurated last Friday. I spoke earlier to France 24’s Maria Clara Calle in Cali, one of the cities affected by the quake.

stories.title: Rare total solar eclipse to cross Europe
stories.summary: We’re just hours away from a rare celestial event: a total solar eclipse. Day will briefly turn to night across parts of northern Spain as the Moon completely blocks out the Sun, while millions more will witness a partial eclipse across Europe, Canada, the northern United States and northwest Africa.

stories.title: Singapore and S Korea pull Trader Joe's seasoning over poppy seeds
stories.summary: Trader Joe's Everything But the Bagel seasoning contains poppy seeds which are banned in both countries.
stories.post: 📰 NEWS: Singapore and S Korea pull Trader Joe's seasoning over poppy seeds. Trader Joe's Everything But the Bagel seasoning contains poppy seeds which are banned in both countries. Source: BBC World.
article_sentences: Singapore and South Korea have pulled Trader Joe's Everything.
But the Bagel seasoning from e-commerce platforms because it contains poppy seeds.
While they do not naturally contain opiates, poppy seeds are banned in both countries because they can get contaminated with opiates by fluid in the poppy plant during harvesting.
More than 20 online listings of the popular seasoning have been removed, Singapore's Central Narcotics Bureau said on Wednesday.
Last week, Seoul authorities said the seasoning tested positive for morphine and codeine, which are opiates found in the plant's sap.
Apart from poppy seeds, the product also contains sesame seeds, sea salt, minced garlic and minced onion.
It was released by American grocery chain Trader Joe's in 2017.
Authorities in Singapore have urged anyone who has bottles of the seasoning to dispose of them.
"Singapore adopts a strict policy of zero tolerance towards controlled drugs," the narcotics bureau said, according to a CNA report.
"The possession, consumption, importation, exportation, manufacturing and trafficking of any controlled drug, even in trace amounts, is an offence under the Misuse of Drugs Act," it said.
In South Korea, investigators say some people brought the seasoning back home as souvenirs from their overseas trips before listing it for resale.
Some did so without realising it contained controlled substances, while others did so knowingly, according to a report by The Korea Herald.
